goal: Read graph.json as exactly {vertices: [unique string IDs], edges: [[from, to], ...]}. Every edge endpoint exists; inputs are directed acyclic graphs with at most 64 vertices, and repeated edges have set semantics. Deliver result/order.json as exactly {order: [vertex IDs]} containing every vertex once, including isolated vertices, in the lexicographically smallest valid topological order using Unicode code-point string order. Separately deliver result/toposort.py: python3 result/toposort.py graph.json prints the same JSON object for that input to stdout. The CLI is required to return stdout, not to create or rewrite result/order.json. It must handle any valid input of this form, including the empty graph, duplicate edges and different vertex/edge orderings. Preserve every supplied input byte; do not modify the input file.

files.result/toposort.py:
import json,sys
document=json.load(open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8'))
remaining=set(document['vertices'])
edges=set(map(tuple,document['edges']))
order=[]
while remaining:
    available=[v for v in remaining if not any(right==v and left in remaining for left,right in edges)]
    item=min(available)
    order.append(item)
    remaining.remove(item)
print(json.dumps({'order':order},ensure_ascii=False,indent=2))
